findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed node's sibling claim does not hold at higher contention. In my contended reproduction (8 CPU spinners, 10 runs at -n 3, loadavg ~75) test_a_discarded_run_is_not_recreated fails 6 of 10 at line 1199 ('the supervisor wrote a pointer for a run that was discarded'), the same assertion the base arm fails at line 1196. The manifest reports this sibling's head arm as 20 pass / 0 fail, which held at its own lower load (~27) but is not robust; the change fixes the pid-read race (line 1145) but not the discard race at line 1199, which the node itself documents as a product-side lost update in follow_ons. This does not block landing, which is correct for the node's named target test.

item_verdicts.diff: base e49e4731a..head 89e4c221c, +17/-5 in one file; swaps pointer-pid reads for output.get('pid') in both supervisor-waiting cases and bounds the exit-record wait by max(EXIT_RECORD_BOUND, launch_seconds * DRIVER_EXIT_SLACK).
item_verdicts.done_when: base fails under contention (run's base-20: 13 pass / 7 fail; my base: 7 pass / 1 fail) and head passes (run's head-20: 20 pass / 0 fail; my head: 8 pass / 0 fail) for the named test; the sibling clause is weaker -- head 6 of 10 fail at line 1199 in my contended run.
item_verdicts.goal: the timing is named with file and line and both supervisor-waiting cases take the pid from the record dispatch returned; the primary case passes 8/8 in my own contended reproduction.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; one commit 89e4c221c, changed_paths correct, base/head contended figures present, negative_control_log names base-20/logs/run-7.log (valid: FAILED id and EXIT=1); negative_control_note cites a wrong base sha 6926b382d.
item_verdicts.write_paths: exactly one committed file, tests/test_dispatch_returns_without_worker.py, inside the declared path; the declared fragment/figure paths legitimately unused under the small-node rule.

justifications.durability: the fix is committed test code and removes the load-sensitive race at its source, so the guard no longer depends on a timing window; the completion wait is bounded by a measured figure. Not higher because the sibling case reading the same pointer still fails at head under contention and the underlying product-side lost update in _mutate_pointer/_publish_stored_phase is deliberately left unfixed (the node documents it as a follow-on).
justifications.evidence: the primary evidence is strong and independently reproduced: from the reviewed run's own base-20 logs (13 pass / 7 fail, two failure modes matching the attribution at lines 1359 and 1369) and by my own contended runs (named test base 7/1, head 8/0); but the manifest's sibling claim 'head 20 of 20' does not reproduce -- at loadavg ~75 test_a_discarded_run_is_not_recreated fails 6 of 10 at line 1199, the same assertion base fails at line 1196 -- and the negative_control_note cites base sha 6926b382d, which is not the reviewed base nor an ancestor of head (the base arm logs name e49e4731a).
justifications.fit: the change reuses the dispatch contract's returned record (pid, dispatch_seconds) rather than adding a new source, reuses the existing DRIVER_EXIT_SLACK constant (line 106), and touches only the two cases that wait on the supervisor; minimal diff, each comment names the race it closes.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the goal is met for the named test: the timing is named with file and line (SUPERVISOR_SURVIVAL_SECONDS = 2.0 at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:9212; EXIT_RECORD_BOUND = 10.0 at tests/test_dispatch_returns_without_worker.py:96), the base arm fails under contention (reproduced 7 pass / 1 fail) and the head arm is robust (reproduced 8 pass / 0 fail at loadavg 75); one point off because the exit-record wait remains a wall-clock window, bounded from the launch dispatch's own measured dispatch_seconds rather than the event itself.
justifications.scope_discipline: only tests/test_dispatch_returns_without_worker.py is changed, +17/-5, inside the declared write path; one commit 89e4c221c with a conventional subject and a body; no plan, state, index or sprint file touched; the declared fragment and figure paths are correctly left unwritten under the small-node landing rule (22 changed lines, done-when names no artifact).
